name: Error Handling
description: Check every returned error, wrap with %w so the cause survives, and treat errors as ordinary values.
cues: errors assigned to _ or silently dropped
fmt.Errorf without %w losing the cause
err logged but execution continues anyway

name: Accept Interfaces, Return Structs
description: Take the narrowest interface that covers what the function needs and hand back concrete types.
cues: concrete parameter where one method is used
exported functions returning interface types
*os.File taken where io.Reader would do

name: Small Interfaces
description: Interfaces stay powerful by staying tiny; a broad interface is hard to satisfy and weakly abstract.
cues: many-method interface with one implementation
interface declared by the producer, not consumer
tests forced to stub methods they never call

name: Useful Zero Value
description: Design types so their zero value works immediately without a constructor call.
cues: type misbehaves unless a New function ran
required Init methods before first use
writes to a nil map waiting to happen

name: Goroutine Leaks
description: Every goroutine needs a known exit path; one that can block forever is a leak.
cues: send on a channel nobody may receive from
worker loop with no done or cancel signal
goroutines spawned per request with no owner

name: Context Propagation
description: Pass context.Context as the first parameter through call chains that do I/O; never store it in a struct.
cues: context.Background() deep inside library code
ctx kept in a struct field
blocking calls that ignore cancellation

name: Defer for Cleanup
description: Acquire a resource and defer its release on the next line so no return path can leak it.
cues: Close or Unlock called on some paths only
release far from the acquisition site
defer inside a loop piling up until exit

name: Table-Driven Tests
description: Express related cases as a table of inputs and expected outputs iterated in one test body.
cues: copy-pasted tests differing only in literals
sequential assertions repeating one pattern
unnamed cases making failures hard to place

name: Package Naming
description: Package names are short, lower-case, and meaningful, and exported names read well with the prefix.
cues: catch-alls named util, common, or helpers
stuttering names like parser.ParseParser
underscores or mixed case in package names

name: Receiver Naming
description: Use the same short receiver identifier on every method of a type, never self or this.
cues: receiver name varies across a type's methods
receivers named self, this, or me
long receiver names shadowed by locals

name: Premature Abstraction
description: Skip layers and interfaces until a second concrete use proves the need; a little copying beats a little dependency.
cues: interface added for one implementation just in case
wrappers around the stdlib adding nothing
deep package tree for a small program

name: Sync Misuse
description: Prefer sharing memory by communicating; when a mutex is needed, keep the critical section small and its ownership obvious.
cues: mutex copied by value or exported
lock held across I/O or channel operations
shared fields with no stated guard

name: Channel Buffering
description: Pick a channel's buffer size deliberately: unbuffered for synchronization, buffered only with a reasoned capacity.
cues: arbitrary sizes like 100 with no rationale
buffer papering over a missing consumer
unbuffered channel causing avoidable deadlock

name: time.After in Loops
description: time.After inside a loop allocates a timer per iteration that lives until it fires; use a Timer or Ticker instead.
cues: time.After in a select inside a for loop
a timer allocated per message on hot paths
long-lived timers never stopped

name: SQL Parameterization
description: Build SQL with placeholder parameters, never by concatenating or formatting user input into the query string.
cues: fmt.Sprintf assembling a query from input
string concatenation of WHERE clauses
query text varying per request
